title: The claim reader's list of names for the rejected cloud routine (`cloud_option.named_as`) has no tripwire at either end: the shipped README's own words for that option ('hosted code routine of the platform', 'sandbox routine against the remote') pass the reader as a mechanism claim (verify round 2 N1, TSK-0133)
observed:
MEASURED 2026-09-11 01:4x by the merge verifier (project_memory/staging/TSK-0133/verify-round-2.md, N1), one sentence inserted into radar/README.md per row, arbiter the whole tools/test_radar_trigger.py:
  * v04 'The hosted code routine of the platform starts the radar-watcher every Friday from the Desktop.' -> GREEN, 9 passed
  * v05 'The platform's sandbox routine against the remote starts the radar-watcher every Friday from the Desktop.' -> GREEN, 9 passed
  * v01 'The claude.ai cloud routine starts the radar-watcher every Friday from the Desktop.' -> RED (the merge's B3 fix)
The reader (tools/test_radar_trigger.py:193-199) refuses first any sentence naming an option whose `built` is false -- derived from the declaration -- but the NAMES of that option are a list, `named_as = ["claude.ai", "cloud routine", "RemoteTrigger"]` (tools/radar_routine.py:338), and the shipped radar/README.md describes the same option in the paragraph 'The rejected alternative' as 'a hosted code routine of the platform, running in a sandbox against the remote' -- two names the list does not carry. House rule 1 (CLAUDE.md): an enumeration without a tripwire that measures both ends.
expected: The names of a not-built option are read from the shipped text that describes it, or the list is measured at both ends: every wording the paragraph 'The rejected alternative' uses for the option is in `named_as` (a missing one is red), and every `named_as` entry occurs in that paragraph (a dead one is red) -- the STALE_LADDER_TEXTS pattern of G5-2. Then a sentence that promotes the rejected option under any of its shipped names is refused whatever else it says.
repro: Insert 'The hosted code routine of the platform starts the radar-watcher every Friday.' into radar/README.md and run tools/test_radar_trigger.py: 9 passed (expected: red).

acceptance_criteria.text: v04 and v05 of verify-round-2.md are RED against the whole tools/test_radar_trigger.py, v01/v02 stay RED, the unmutated README stays GREEN
the two-ended tripwire exists: a name used by the 'rejected alternative' paragraph but absent from named_as is red; a named_as entry the paragraph does not use is red
the reader's docstring says what it reads (the declaration's names, measured against the shipped paragraph), no more

limits: No protection is lost today: the shipped README makes no cloud claim, and the three listed names catch the phrasings anyone has actually typed (m10, v01, v02). What is open is the class -- a future text that promotes the rejected option under its own README wording is not refused. Until closed, the round that changes radar/README.md re-runs the verifier's v04/v05 rows by hand (the rows stand in verify-round-2.md).
